answer: Soil-probe grove check: each identity plants one $49 moisture probe in its own hollow of a registered meadow grove, GPS-pinned in the county land trust's public plot registry. Each epoch the probe signs its soil reading; the verifier matches it against NOAA's public rain-gauge record for that cell — a reading that contradicts the rain fails, and two identities sharing one probe publish identical readings and both fail. One probe cannot water two groves, so a farm must buy and plant new hardware for every fake.
